title: Blvck Motorbike: bikes, prices and how to rent (2026)
description: Blvck Motorbike's bikes and daily prices, the licence class each bike needs, and what to ask about deposit, papers and delivery before you ride away.
h1: Blvck Motorbike in Ho Chi Minh City: bikes, daily prices and how to rent one
intro: Blvck Motorbike is a motorbike rental company at 57 Pasteur in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City. It rents scooters and semi-automatic bikes by the day or by the month and delivers across the city. It does not publish a deposit amount or a document list for foreign renters, so ask about both before you pay. Daily prices are in the table below.
keyPoints: Blvck Motorbike is an official eno.vn partner. Since 4 November 2026 it has been the only motorbike rental on eno.vn, and its storefront is at [/blvck](/blvck).
According to Blvck Motorbike's own website, as of November 2026, daily prices run from {{vnd:100000}} for a Honda Wave or Yamaha Sirius to {{vnd:500000}} for a Honda SH 150cc.
Blvck publishes **no deposit amount, no document list for foreigners and no delivery fee**. Get all three in writing before you pay anything.
Under Law 36/2024/QH15, Article 57, a class A1 licence covers bikes up to 125cc. The Honda SH 150cc needs class A.
Blvck's site says it delivers anywhere in the city, inner and outer areas alike, gives you two helmets with each bike and offers monthly rentals.

blocks.text: **Blvck Motorbike is a motorbike rental business in Ho Chi Minh City.** It rents out semi-automatic bikes and scooters by the day, the week or the month, and it delivers them to your address. Its Vietnamese-language website, [thuexemaysaigon.vn](https://thuexemaysaigon.vn/), gives its address as 57 Pasteur, Ben Nghe, District 1. The same site says customers have trusted it "over the past 10 years".

On eno.vn, Blvck Motorbike is an official partner. Since 4 November 2026 it has been the only motorbike rental on the site, and its storefront is at [eno.vn/blvck](/blvck). The storefront is where you pick a bike and message the shop.

A [December 2024 article in Báo Đồng Nai](https://baodongnai.com.vn/doanh-nhan-doanh-nghiep/dich-vu/202412/dich-vu-thue-xe-may-blvck-motorbike-gia-re-o-sai-gon-17e54f5/) listed 21 branches. They were spread across Tan Binh, Phu Nhuan, Districts 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12, Go Vap, Tan Phu and Binh Thanh. The company's own site no longer lists them, so ask which branch will hand over your bike.

A note on addresses: Ho Chi Minh City has had no official districts since 1 July 2025, and official addresses now use new ward names. Shops and riders still say "District 1" or "Go Vap", and this guide does the same.

sections.title: How much does Blvck Motorbike charge?

blocks.text: According to Blvck Motorbike's own website, as of November 2026, a semi-automatic bike costs {{vnd:100000}} a day. Everyday scooters cost {{vnd:150000}} a day, and the premium scooters cost {{vnd:300000-500000}} a day. These are the prices the site showed on 22 November 2026, and they can change.

blocks.text: The eno.vn storefront at [/blvck](/blvck) shows the bikes it lists and their prices at the time you look. When you agree a price in the chat, quote the listing you are booking from.

blocks.title: Crossed-out prices
blocks.text: Blvck's site shows a higher "original" price struck through next to each current price. For example, the Honda Vision showed {{vnd:250000}} struck through beside {{vnd:150000}}. The banner also says "from 80K a day", but on 22 November 2026 no bike on the site was priced below {{vnd:100000}}. Agree the actual figure in writing.
Is it cheaper to rent by the month?

Probably, but Blvck prints no monthly price list. Its booking form lets you pick 1, 2, 3 or more than 3 months. On 22 November 2026 the site also showed a sample booking for a Honda Wave Alpha for one month at {{vnd:1500000}}. That was one customer's booking notice, not a published tariff. If you will ride to work every day, ask for a monthly quote. Then compare it with buying a used bike in [Vehicles](/c/vehicles).

sections.title: How do I rent a bike from Blvck Motorbike?

blocks.text: Choose a bike on the [Blvck Motorbike storefront](/blvck) and message the shop in eno.vn chat. Give your dates and your delivery address. Blvck's own site says a booking takes about two minutes. Still, message a day or so ahead if you need the bike at a set time.

items.title: Choose a bike your licence covers
items.text: Match the bike to the licence class you actually hold (see the table above). A small scooter or a Wave is enough for city commuting.

items.title: Message the shop on eno.vn
items.text: Sign in, open [/blvck](/blvck) and use the chat. Give the model, your dates or number of months, and where the bike should go.

items.title: Get the terms in writing
items.text: Ask for the total price, the deposit and when it comes back, and the documents they need from a foreign renter. Also ask about the delivery fee and who pays for damage, theft or an impounded bike.

items.title: Check the bike at handover
items.text: Film the bike all round. Check the plate against the registration certificate, test the brakes, horn and lights, and make sure both helmets fit.

items.title: Return it as agreed
items.text: Bring the bike back on time with the fuel you received. Get your deposit back before the staff leave, or a written reason for any deduction.

blocks.text: Keeping the whole arrangement in one eno.vn chat gives you a written record of the price and terms. For the general handover checks and how deposits work in the city, see [renting a motorbike in Ho Chi Minh City](/motorbike-rental-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: What deposit and documents does Blvck Motorbike need?

blocks.text: Blvck Motorbike does not publish a deposit amount or a document list for foreign renters, so ask in the chat. Get the answer in writing before you hand over money or any document.

Here is what the published sources do say. On 22 November 2026, Blvck's own site promised a "low deposit" (đặt cọc thấp). It also said the shop keeps the renter's citizen ID card (căn cước công dân), which only Vietnamese customers have. Its booking form asks whether you already hold a driving licence. The 2024 Báo Đồng Nai article said either a citizen ID or a licence was enough. Neither source says what a foreigner should leave, so ask.

blocks.title: Keep your original passport
blocks.text: Offer a photocopy or a cash deposit instead, and get a receipt that shows the amount and when it will be returned. A bank, a landlord or your employer may ask to see your passport at short notice.
Does Blvck Motorbike deliver the bike?

Yes. According to Blvck's site, as of November 2026, the shop delivers to any address in the city's inner and outer areas, and each bike comes with two helmets. The site also says there are no extra service fees and that help is available 24/7 if something goes wrong. The 2024 article also mentioned a raincoat and "full insurance". The current site mentions neither, so ask whether a raincoat comes with the bike and which insurance certificate it carries.

sections.title: Which licence do I need to ride a Blvck rental?

blocks.text: For most bikes in Blvck's fleet you need a class A1 licence, which covers two-wheelers up to 125cc. The Honda SH 150cc needs class A. [Article 57 of Law 36/2024/QH15](https://hethongphapluat.com/luat-trat-tu-an-toan-giao-thong-duong-bo-2024/dieu-57) sets A1 at a cylinder capacity of up to 125cc, or an electric motor of up to 11 kW. Class A covers anything larger.

The same article accepts some foreign licences. It covers a licence issued under a treaty Vietnam has joined, if it matches the type of vehicle. It also covers an international driving permit from a 1968 Vienna Convention country, carried with your valid home licence. Both must cover the class of bike you ride. An international permit cannot outlast the home licence that goes with it. To find out whether your permit counts, see [the international driving permit in Vietnam](/guides/international-driving-permit-vietnam).

A rental shop does not decide whether you are riding legally. The licence you hold decides that. If you are staying long term, a Vietnamese licence is the lasting answer: see [getting a motorbike licence in Vietnam as a foreigner](/teach-in-vietnam/motorbike-licence-in-vietnam-for-foreigners).

sections.title: Is renting from Blvck Motorbike a good choice?

blocks.text: Blvck Motorbike suits you if you want a bike delivered to your address, with a choice of models and the deal set out in writing in one chat. If you only make short trips, or you do not yet hold a licence that covers the bike, ride-hailing or the metro may suit you better.

items: **Your first weeks in the city:** rent a Wave or a Vision by the day or week while you learn your routes. See [getting around Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-around-ho-chi-minh-city).
**Staying for months:** ask for a monthly quote and compare it with buying a used bike in [Vehicles](/c/vehicles).
**Bigger scooters:** the SH 150cc is comfortable for longer rides but needs class A. Check the cc of any premium scooter on its registration before you ride.
**Electric instead:** for VinFast's own rental scooters, see [VinFast rental in Ho Chi Minh City](/guides/vinfast-electric-scooter-and-car-rental-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: Renting outside Ho Chi Minh City, in Hanoi, Da Nang or elsewhere. See [motorbike rental in Vietnam](/guides/renting-a-motorbike-in-vietnam).
Traffic fines and what to do after an accident. See the [Ho Chi Minh City motorbike rental guide](/guides/renting-a-motorbike-in-ho-chi-minh-city).
Blvck Motorbike's insurance cover, damage charges and refund terms. They are not published, so ask the shop in eno.vn chat and keep the answer.

faqs.a: Blvck Motorbike is a motorbike rental company in Ho Chi Minh City, based at 57 Pasteur in District 1. It rents Honda and Yamaha semi-automatics and scooters, plus Vespa and SH models, by the day or by the month. It delivers bikes to addresses across the city. Blvck Motorbike is an official eno.vn partner, with a storefront at eno.vn/blvck.

faqs.q: How much is Blvck Motorbike per day?
faqs.a: Blvck Motorbike's daily price depends on the bike. A Honda Wave or Yamaha Sirius is the cheapest, everyday scooters like the Vision or Lead cost a little more, and the Honda SH 150cc costs the most. The exact figures, as read on Blvck's own website on 22 November 2026, are in the price table above. Blvck Motorbike quotes monthly rates on request.

faqs.q: How do I book Blvck Motorbike?
faqs.a: To book Blvck Motorbike through eno.vn, sign in, open the Blvck Motorbike storefront at eno.vn/blvck and message the shop in the chat. Give the model you want, your dates or number of months and your delivery address. Before you pay, ask Blvck Motorbike to confirm the total price, the deposit, the documents it needs and any delivery fee in writing.

faqs.q: Does Blvck Motorbike require a deposit?
faqs.a: Blvck Motorbike does not publish a deposit amount for foreign renters. Its website promises a low deposit and says it keeps the renter's Vietnamese citizen ID card, which foreigners do not have. Ask Blvck Motorbike in the chat how much the deposit is, what it accepts instead of an original passport and when you get the deposit back. Get a receipt.

Yes. Blvck Motorbike's website says it delivers rental bikes to any address in Ho Chi Minh City, in both inner and outer areas, and supplies two helmets with each bike. The website names no delivery fee and says there are no extra service charges. Ask Blvck Motorbike to confirm in writing that delivery to your address is included, and when the bike will arrive.

faqs.q: What licence do I need to rent a Honda SH from Blvck Motorbike?
faqs.a: The Honda SH 150cc that Blvck Motorbike rents is over 125cc, so in Vietnam it needs a class A licence under Article 57 of Law 36/2024/QH15. A class A1 licence covers only bikes up to 125cc. A foreigner may instead carry an international driving permit from a 1968 Vienna Convention country, together with a valid home licence that covers that class.
